decisions.reason: As a reference-class electrometer that stayed on the home page in both 2023 and 2024, it appears highly aligned with the firm's core measurement know-how and worth refining rather than withdrawing.

The oncology risk management software remained on its own page across 2023 and 2024, but because software is somewhat less central than physical QA instruments to this firm's likely knowledge base, it carries a higher—though still minority—withdrawal risk.
A CT image quality test phantom fits closely with established imaging QA capabilities, so under an absorptive-capacity logic the firm is likely to learn from early use and keep it on the market.
The mammography image quality phantom is strongly related to the firm's apparent medical imaging test expertise, making continued commercialization and incremental improvement more likely than exit.
A full field mammography test phantom is a specialized but still core-adjacent QA product, so the firm is likely to retain it unless first-year demand proves clearly insufficient.
Medical imaging quality assurance instruments sit at the center of the firm's likely technical and market knowledge, which makes withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.
